messages:
alex: Evening handoff — quick notes and things to watch

alex: TL;DR: prod is green after the 18:10 runtime tweak. Small spike in tail latency after the change (0.9% -> 1.8% p99), rolled back at 18:35. No customer-facing errors observed.

alex: What changed
- rolled a config tweak that enabled continuous-batching: max_batch_size=64 -> 128 for raw-gen workers.
- quantize-nightly job triggered on a subset of models (~3:00AM UTC) still scheduled, no action taken yet.
- embeddings cluster had 5% higher mem pressure during the spike; likely coincident with a large reindex job.

alex: What to watch
- p99 latency on /v1/generate (prod) — paging threshold 500ms; we saw short blips up to ~620ms.
- worker GPU queue length for node-group infer-q2 (dashboard: infra -> GPUs -> infer-q2).
- KV cache miss rate — if miss rate climbs >8% for 10m, flip fallback to smaller KV shard (see runbook).

alex: Action items for tonight
- @jamie please keep an eye on the GPU queue between 22:00–02:00 UTC (possible batch patterns).
- @priya I left a CR for the rollback doc, please merge and tag oncall-runbook.
- If tail latency >700ms for 5m, escalate to eng-runtime and start rolling back continuous-batching config immediately.

jamie: Ack. I can monitor dashboards. If I see queue depth >120, I'll scale down incoming concurrency and notify.

jamie: Question — should we pause the quantize-nightly tomorrow while we investigate? It's scheduled at 03:00 and touches the same model family.

alex: Yes, pause it for one night. I don't want overlapping resource pressure while we look at patterns. To pause: run this in infra cluster:

```
kubectl -n infra scale cronjob/quantize-nightly --replicas=0
```

alex: Then re-enable after 06:00 UTC with replicas=1.

priya: I adjusted the KV-cache alert earlier because we were getting noisy false positives from one shard. I raised the threshold from 5% -> 8% miss-rate for alerts; changed the alert description to call out shard id. I left a note in the alert's runbook.

alex: Thanks @priya — that's fine. Please add the shard id to the pager message so folks know which shard.

priya: Done. Also FYI I pushed a small tweak to the telemetry sidecar to drop a noisy debug log that'll reduce log volume during spikes. Shouldn't affect any metrics.

oncall-bot: [deploy-bot] Deployment completed: runtime-config v2026.02.18-137 (rolled back) — triggered at 18:10, reverted at 18:35. No new incidents opened.

liam: I can cover 23:00–03:00 UTC if you want extra hands. Happy to take pagers if needed.

alex: Appreciate it. @liam — if you see repeated 503s on /v1/embed, check the tokenizer process (recent CPU surge) and respawn the tokenizer workers if CPU stays >85% for 2 minutes. Command to restart tokenizer workers:

```
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/tokenizer-workers
```

alex: Final notes
- No customer tickets opened related to this spike — reached out to a couple of engaged users and they reported no degradation.
- Cost: minor spike on token compute last hour, watch the cost dashboard tomorrow morning.
- If anything weird shows up, add to the #incidents channel and ping me and @jamie.

jamie: Got it. I'll monitor and keep this thread updated if anything changes. :thumbsup:

priya: I'll follow up in the morning with a short postmortem candidate if we see another blip.

liam: On it — will DM if I take the pager.

oncall-bot: Reminder scheduled: oncall-handoff-check @ 22:55 UTC
